slug: 2026-01-13 Cameroon intros digital system for civil documents

facts.fact: ITWeb Africa, citing UNDP, says the digital civil status system covers ten municipalities in the Far North, North-West and South-West: Maroua III, Koza, Mindif, Meri, Mora, Limbe I, Buea City Council, Tiko, Bamenda III and Bamenda City Council; no national total is given and the coverage is undated, so the date is the publication date.
facts.system: digital civil status system at council level (UNDP)

facts.fact: ITWeb Africa says the system lets birth, marriage and death certificates be securely issued, stored and retrieved at council level; Limbe I's civil status chief says a birth certificate no longer takes three hand-filled pages; date is the publication date.
facts.system: digital civil status system at council level (UNDP)

facts.fact: ITWeb Africa reports in January 2026 that Cameroon has introduced a digital system for processing and archiving civil status records at council level, in ten municipalities of three regions, with Limbe I pioneering it in the South-West.
facts.system: digital civil status system at council level (UNDP)

facts.fact: The initiative is implemented by UNDP, per ITWeb Africa; no national registration body is named in the captured text; date is the publication date.
facts.system: digital civil status system at council level (UNDP)

facts.fact: The initiative is funded by Denmark through the UNDP Funding Windows, per ITWeb Africa; date is the publication date.
facts.system: digital civil status system at council level (UNDP)
